text: One action exports the router's recent log, every declared upstream with its live state and cached tool surface, and the recent tool calls — and no credential value leaves in it. A secret-bearing field is never placed in the document; every known secret value is removed from every string that does survive, in its literal, percent-encoded and base64 forms; a value too short to be scrubbed from free text is named rather than used; and the untokened preview carries counts and no content.

Witnessed by scripts/acceptance/r22-diagnostics.sh, which plants a credential literal in a real servers.json and a real router.log, drives the route over the daemon's own socket, and requires the plant to be provably present on disk before any absence in the reply counts.
note:
R22. The requirement is written as an honesty guardrail rather than a behaviour because the load-bearing half is a promise about what is NOT in the output, and this campaign's own history is that such a promise is satisfied trivially by producing nothing. Every case under it therefore pairs its absence with a presence: a public canary in the same log line, the key names, and a non-zero `occurrencesRemoved`.

R25 (server configuration profile export with safe secret redaction) is the sibling and had NOT landed when this was built — checked at LEDGER.md, status To Do — so the redactor is new here rather than a second one. It is deliberately a general component under RouterCore/Diagnostics rather than private to the bundle, so R25 reuses it instead of writing a third.

text: The router says when an upstream's credential is running out or has been refused, before a tool call fails on it — and it can say that it does not know. Expiry is DERIVED from what the router already holds (`authorizedAt` + `expires_in` in the record it wrote when the flow settled), never asked of the upstream, so nothing is spawned to answer the question. A token whose record declares no lifetime reads `unknown` carrying the reason, and there is no path from a missing number to `valid`. A configured value the router will not take is reported as refused with its scope rather than clamped in silence. Repetition is throttled and escalation is not: a warning becoming an expiry, and an expiry moving because the credential was replaced, go out at once, and re-authorising CLEARS the warning rather than ageing it out.
provider: app/Sources/RouterCore/AuthExpiry/AuthExpiryRecord.swift derives the state and app/Sources/RouterCore/AuthExpiry/AuthExpiryMonitor.swift holds the throttle; app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/ControlAuthExpiry.swift serves both routes on the loopback control listener bound by RouterService, which is the inbound socket this row names. Witnessed by scripts/acceptance/r26-auth-expiry.sh, which plants credential records on disk in a scratch home, drives the routes over the daemon's own socket, and PAIRS every zero-children reading with a reading that moves when the planted file moves — an absence asserted alone is satisfied by a feature that does nothing.
note: R26. It inherits R27's rule (REQ-029) and meets it by not needing it: a health probe of a stdio upstream IS a child process, so R27 defaults background probing off and never lets a scheduled sweep cold-start. An expiry needs no probe at all, so this feature arms no task, holds no timer and spawns nothing — which is why it is ON by default where health probing is off. The vacuity rule is `warnWithinMs`'s floor of 60000 with zero REFUSED: at zero a token passes straight from valid to expired, `expiring` is unreachable, and the promise 'you are told before it stops working' would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names. R27's tripAfter floor of 2 is the same rule one item earlier. The `mobbin` lesson is carried into the notification rather than rediscovered: with a refresh token held, no command is offered, because telling its owner to re-authorise sends them round a loop that cannot succeed.
